root_cause: The radios component only responds to click events, not keyboard-driven change events. When a user navigates with arrow keys to the opt-out radio (which lacks aria-controls), the previously selected radio's conditional field remains visible because no change handler updates aria-expanded and visibility for all radios with aria-controls.
repair_strategy: Add a change event listener that invokes setAttributes on every radio with aria-controls whenever any radio's checked state changes. This ensures conditionals are shown/hidden correctly for both mouse and keyboard interactions.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate the radio group with arrow keys and see dependent fields appear/disappear correctly, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: Possible duplicate execution of setAttributes when both click and change events fire for the same interaction.
If another script depends on the change event not being observed, adding the listener could cause unintended side effects.
Minimal performance overhead from traversing the radio list on each change event.
verification_requirements: Verify that selecting each radio option via keyboard updates the visibility of its associated conditional field correctly.
Verify that clicking a radio option continues to work as before.
Verify that ARIA attributes (aria-controls, aria-expanded) are correctly updated on both click and keyboard selection.
Ensure no regression in existing visual behavior for mouse users.
